title: Osteoarthritis and fibroblast activation: an imaging study assessing feasibility and reliability of whole-body  68  Ga-FAPI PET-CT for structural osteoarthritis evaluation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Osteoarthritis and fibroblast activation: an imaging study assessing feasibility and reliability of whole-body  68  Ga-FAPI PET-CT for structural osteoarthritis evaluation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par8】Thus, the primary aim of this feasibility study was to assess whether presence of OA, as evaluated by multi-joint, multi-anatomy ordinal grading on whole-body CT (using the CT component of 68 Ga-FAPI PET-CT), is associated with 68 Ga-FAPI PET tracer uptake (SUVmax) as a measure of fibroblastic activity. Secondary aims were to evaluate whether OA disease severity is positively correlated with increased tracer uptake and to determine inter- and intra-reader reliability of ordinal whole-body OA assessment on CT and of quantitative SUVmax measurements.

【Objective · abstract-1-1】Primary aim was to evaluate whether presence of osteoarthritis (OA), as assessed by ordinal grading on whole-body computed tomography (CT), is associated with 68 Ga fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) positron emission tomography (PET) tracer uptake as a measure of fibroblastic activation. Secondary aim was to evaluate whether OA disease severity is positively correlated with increased tracer uptake and to evaluate reliability.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Osteoarthritis and fibroblast activation: an imaging study assessing feasibility and reliability of whole-body  68  Ga-FAPI PET-CT for structural osteoarthritis evaluation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient sample and inclusion · Par9】In this single-center retrospective cross-sectional study design, we included adult patients who had undergone 68 Ga-FAPI PET-CT for a spectrum of clinical reasons between March 2018 and June 2024. Included were all available patients who had consented to their imaging data being used for retrospective analysis. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Friedrich-Alexander-Universität (FAU) Erlangen-Nürnberg (#23–359-Bp).

【Patient sample and inclusion · Par10】Main reasons for referral were (1) assessment of structural disease activity in patients with a known inflammatory rheumatologic disorder affecting synovial joints like RA, spondylarthritis (SpA), or psoriatic arthritis (PsA), or (2) patients who were imaged for work-up of a suspected inflammatory disorder, who subsequently did not fulfill diagnostic disease criteria or underwent 68 Ga-FAPI PET-CT for staging of pancreatic cancer. Acute or subacute musculoskeletal trauma (within the last 6 months) was an exclusion criterion. We grouped these patients into three distinct subgroups: (1) those with a diagnosed inflammatory disorder and no concomitant OA (i.e., “inflamed group”), (2) those with a diagnosed inflammatory disorder and concomitant OA (i.e., “mixed group”), and (3) those with no inflammatory disorder (i.e., “non-inflamed group”). The differentiation between groups 1 and 2 was based on the presence or absence of at least 3 joints and/or spine levels with at least early-moderate OA (i.e., at least a definite osteophyte or definite disc space narrowing) on screening the CT images by one of the last authors (A.M.R.).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Osteoarthritis and fibroblast activation: an imaging study assessing feasibility and reliability of whole-body  68  Ga-FAPI PET-CT for structural osteoarthritis evaluation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · Par24】Table 1 presents the associations between structural OA presence (using absence of OA as the referent) and the odds of increased FAPI uptake defined as the highest tertile of mean SUVmax values for the entire sample. Increased odds of increased tracer uptake were observed for both acromioclavicular joints (left: odds ratio (OR) 8.9, 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.8, 44.9]; right: OR 12.5, 95% CI [3.0, 52.8]), for the spine cervical 1 location (OR 5.7, 95% CI [1.6, 20.4]), and for both lumbar spine locations (spine lumbar 1: OR 8.3, 95% CI [1.5, 46.6]; spine lumbar 2: OR 5.0, 95% CI [1.3, 18.7]).

【Results · Par25】Table 2 shows the correlation analyses between structural OA disease severity and SUVmax tracer uptake. Most correlations were small or medium with high correlations > 0.5 seen for both acromioclavicular joints (left: OR 0.56, 95% CI [0.34, 0.73]; right: OR 0.61, 95% CI [0.41, 0.76]), left (OR 0.77, 95% CI [0.44, 0.92]) and right (OR 0.59, 95% CI [0.06, 0.87]) DIP, and right PIP (OR 0.52, 95% CI [0.06, 0.80]) joints for hands. Figure 5 shows a more detailed graphic visualization in exemplary fashion for the right acromioclavicular joint and the spine lumbar 1 location for the entire sample and the different subgroups. On an individual basis and in exemplary cases, definite or severe OA and increased tracer uptake were seen for patients with and without underlying inflammatory disease. An example of structural hip OA and marked concomitant FAPI activity in a patient without inflammatory disorder and in a different patient with knee OA and an established diagnosis of peripheral spondylarthritis and corresponding FAPI activity is shown in Fig. 6.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Osteoarthritis and fibroblast activation: an imaging study assessing feasibility and reliability of whole-body  68  Ga-FAPI PET-CT for structural osteoarthritis evaluation》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · Fig1】Fig. 1 Acromioclavicular joint. Sixty-four-year-old male patient with no history of inflammatory disorder. FAPI tracer uptake was commonly observed in all disease categories. a CT image shows minor signs of osteoarthritis at the left acromioclavicular joint with an osteophyte (arrows) and capsular thickening (arrowhead). b Corresponding fusion image shows moderate FAPI tracer uptake (SUVmax 3.28) at the lateral clavicle without corresponding structural pathology on CT (arrows), a finding of unknown clinical or structural relevance reflecting fibroblastic activity

【Fig. 2 · Fig2】Fig. 2 Ankle. Fifty-seven-year-old male patient with absence of known inflammatory arthritis. a Coronal reformation of CT shows marked joint space narrowing of the central tibiotalar joint (short arrows) and a small subchondral cyst (arrowhead) characteristic of advanced OA. In addition, there are osteophytes at the medial tibiotalar margin (large arrows). b Corresponding coronal fusion image with FAPI PET shows mild tracer uptake (SUV of 2.23) at the medial talar shoulder and corresponding tibial joint in a subchondral location (arrow). c Forty-eight-year-old female patient with known spondylarthritis. While there are no obvious signs of OA, there is marked tracer uptake around the posterior tibialis tendon (arrows) and also in the inferior aspects of the sinus tarsi (arrowhead), most likely due to tenosynovitis and entheseal inflammation

【Fig. 3 · Fig3】Fig. 3 Spine. Sixty-year-old female patient without inflammatory disorder. a Sagittal reformat of the lumbar spine shows marked degenerative disc disease at the L2/L3 level. There is marked intervertebral space narrowing with endplate irregularities, subchondral sclerosis (arrowheads), and anterior osteophytes (arrows). b Corresponding fusion image shows increased tracer uptake in the peridiscal location at the L2 and L3 endplates. In addition, there is anterior uptake at the location of the osteophytes. Tracer uptake was moderate with an SUVmax of 2.96
